request: Can you pull the reactions that Tom added on our recent roadmap-planning messages? I want to see what he reacted to.

selection_plan.focal_condition: users.real_name = "Tom" (route node_index 1, the USER endpoint of the reaction's authoring user)
auxiliary_conditions: Reaction's message lies within the supplied roadmap-planning audit scope: two named channels, one per workspace, both readable by the actor
Emoji/context is an ordinary planning-reaction (no arbitrary extra qualifier beyond scope membership)
selection_plan.candidate_scope: All reactions on messages inside the two audit-scope channels (one channel in Workspace A, one in Workspace B), each channel's members and message/reaction history fully paginated and readable by the actor.
selection_plan.criteria_count: Focal (real_name="Tom") plus one auxiliary (channel-scope membership); within limit of three.

resolution_plan.rationale: Two distinct users independently satisfy real_name="Tom": one in the Workspace A channel, one in the Workspace B channel. Each has added a genuine reaction inside the audit scope, so 'the reaction Tom added' resolves to two different, non-overlapping reaction identities (different message_id/user_id/emoji triples) rather than two paths converging on one reaction.
competing_singletons: Reaction R_A: Tom (real_name="Tom", Workspace A) on a roadmap message in Channel A
Reaction R_B: Tom (real_name="Tom", Workspace B) on a roadmap message in Channel B
resolution_plan.no_authority_to_choose: The request gives no distinguishing detail (no username, workspace, or message content) that would let the actor pick between the two Toms, so both remain live candidates.

negative_plan.near_miss_type: focal near-miss (relationship/attribute near-miss on the same route)
negative_plan.design: A third user, real_name "Thomas Reyes" but display_name "Tom", also reacts on a roadmap message inside one of the two audit-scope channels (satisfying the auxiliary scope condition). Because the focal condition binds strictly to users.real_name, this reaction fails the focal criterion even though casual reference to 'Tom' plausibly points to this display name too.
negative_plan.plausibility: The near-miss reaction sits in the same channel/workspace as one of the true Toms, on a similarly-themed roadmap message, so it cannot be excluded by scope or topic alone—only by checking the real_name field.
negative_plan.accidental_match_check: Confirm Thomas Reyes has no other real_name alias of exactly "Tom"; confirm no fourth user with real_name "Tom" exists outside the two intended channels who would silently add a third competing candidate.

environment_plan: Two workspaces, each containing one active roadmap-planning channel readable by the actor (actor holds membership enabling access per users.info scope rules). Channel A (Workspace A) hosts a handful of ordinary roadmap messages; one is authored by a regular contributor and reacted to by the first 'Tom' (real_name exactly 'Tom'). Channel B (Workspace B) similarly hosts roadmap messages; one is reacted to by the second 'Tom' (a distinct user, also real_name exactly 'Tom', different user_id/workspace). Channel A additionally contains a second roadmap message reacted to by 'Thomas Reyes' (display_name 'Tom') as the near-miss, keeping it in-scope by channel but out-of-scope by real_name. Filler messages/users/reactions (a few unrelated contributors with unrelated names) round out ordinary channel activity without introducing extra real_name='Tom' matches. All created_at timestamps set explicitly and distinctly to keep ordering deterministic.
action_plan: 1. Read message_reactions joined to users for Channel A and Channel B (per Card #1) to find all reactions where the associated user's real_name is 'Tom'. 2. Because two disjoint, equally-supported reactions (one per workspace/channel) satisfy this, report both candidate reactions as the underspecified answer rather than selecting one; explicitly flag the Thomas Reyes reaction as excluded (fails focal real_name condition) if it surfaces during the channel-scoped read.
